text:
maya: Hey team — partner sent a new model bundle (llama-x-3b-v1). Before we start evals we need a clear artifact provenance + registry ingest checklist. Who can summarize required files and verification steps?

<todd>: Quick checklist draft: weights, tokenizer, model config, license, model card, checksums, signature. small README with source URL.

anika: Agree. Concrete filenames we require in the upload: 
- model.safetensors OR model.pt (prefer safetensors)
- tokenizer.json or tokenizer.model (sentencepiece)
- config.json
- README.md (incl license text or link)
- provenance.json (metadata, see example below)
- model.sha256 (single-line sha256 of the weight file)
- model.safetensors.sig OR model.pt.sig (PGP detached sig)

<todd>: Example provenance.json (one-line in the upload):
```json
{"source": "https://huggingface.co/org/llama-x", "commit": "a1b2c3d4", "downloaded_by": "partner-acme", "download_date": "2026-03-01T12:00:00Z", "license": "proprietary:acme-contracted"}
```

<ryan>: In addition to file list, registry fields we need: model_id, semantic_version, arch, tokenizer_type, precision, tags, canonical_weight_sha256, signed_by (PGP key id), provenance_url (S3), retention_days. Example tag scheme: llama-x:v1, arch:decoder-only, precision:f32.

<security-bot>: Required security checks: verify sha256, verify PGP detached signature (we trust known partner PGP keys stored in vault), and confirm license compatibility with customer SLA. Use KMS key for storage encryption.

<ci-bot>: Ingest pipeline expects this s3 layout (upload to inbound prefix):
`s3://redwood-models-inbound/<team-or-partner>/<model_id>/<version>/`
Example: `s3://redwood-models-inbound/acme/llama-x/1.0.0/`
Files validated by ingest lambda: model.*, tokenizer.*, provenance.json, *.sig, *.sha256 -> then moved to canonical bucket `s3://redwood-models-canonical/` with path `/<model_id>/<version>/<artifact>` and registry entry created.

<anika>: Verification commands we run (include in docs):
```bash
sha256sum model.safetensors  # compare to model.sha256
gpg --verify model.safetensors.sig model.safetensors  # check detached signature against partner key
# optional: pip install safetensors && python -c "import safetensors; print('ok')"
```
If signature fails, we quarantine and notify security.

<todd>: Quantized variants: store as separate versioned artifacts but link in registry manifest. Naming convention: `<model_id>-<version>-quant-<bits>-<method>.safetensors` e.g., `llama-x-1.0.0-quant-4-awq.safetensors`. Registry entry should include `canonical_weight_sha256` (for canonical float weights) and `quant_variants: [ {name, sha256, precision, method, quant_date}]`.

<ryan>: Storage class + retention: canonical weights => GLACIER_DEEP_ARCHIVE? no, we keep hot for 90 days in STANDARD then transition to STANDARD_IA. Quantized artifacts: STANDARD for 30 days then archive. All moved objects must be encrypted with customer/service KMS: `arn:aws:kms:us-west-2:123456789012:key/xxxx`. Access control: group `eng-ml-models`, plus explicit ACL for partner SSO if needed.

<security-bot>: Also add registry metadata flags: `signed:true`, `license_checked:true`, `provenance_verified:true`, `supply_chain_level: sca-1`. That drives RBAC and canary rollout policies.

<maya>: Nice. A couple of operational notes:
- ingestion will auto-create registry draft entry but a human must approve `license_checked` and `provenance_verified` before dedicated infra rollout.
- please include a short prompt/testset in `/evals/` with expected outputs or failure modes.

<todd>: Minimal prompt/testset naming: `llama-x-1.0.0-smoke.jsonl` (first 100 prompts) — store under same version folder in `evals/` so optimize pipeline can pick it up.

<anika>: I'll add small doc snippet to repo `infra/model-ingest/README.md` with the required filename list, verification commands, s3 prefixes, and example provenance.json.

<ryan>: One more: registry keys for automation: `ingest_id`, `artifact_path`, `ingest_time`, `ingested_by` (S3 principal), `signature_key_id`. Keep values immutable once signed.

<maya>: OK — action items: Anika will add README + update ingest lambda to enforce .sig presence. Todd will draft the registry manifest template. Ryan will add storage lifecycle policy. Security-bot to confirm partner PGP key is in vault. I'll open an intake ticket linking this thread.

<todd>: on it. :white_check_mark:

<anika>: starting now, will ping when PR is up.

<security-bot>: partner key present? not yet — requesting key upload from partner.

<maya>: Thanks — keeping this thread as the canonical discussion for provenance/registry for this model. I'll post ticket number once created.

<ci-bot>: ingest smoke run scheduled after human approval will be: `ingest-service --path s3://redwood-models-inbound/acme/llama-x/1.0.0/ --dry-run`

<maya>: Assigning intake ticket to @todd and @anika for next 48h.

<ryan>: FYI I'll add a small alert if signature verification fails more than once for same partner to detect misconfig or supply-chain issues.

<maya:> Thanks all — thread closed for now unless we need more details.
